display.purpose: Page-level titles. Rare — two uses in the whole build.

body.purpose: The 15px UI base; row titles and summaries.

micro.purpose: 12px floor: paths, counts, state words, chip labels. Most-used utility.

mono.purpose: Code, paths, IDs, commands, measurements only. Ligatures off.

materials.name: material-chrome
materials.purpose: App header, rail header, thumb bar. Night: oklch(0.205 0.008 60 / 0.72).

materials.name: material-panel

materials.name: reduced-transparency-fallback

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Inputs, in-transcript cards, kbd hints. Night: 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.30).

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Default for a card on the canvas: board sections, attention queue. Night: 0 2px 8px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.38), 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.28).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Popovers and floating docks. Night: 0 8px 28px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.46), 0 2px 8px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.32).

shadows.name: shadow-xl

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entrances and state changes; approximates a critically damped spring.

motion.name: ease-inout-soft
motion.purpose: Reversible position swaps only (card → header morphs, 240ms).

motion.name: ease-phone-push
motion.purpose: Horizontal page pushes on phones, 200ms, direction from html[data-nav].

motion.name: duration-large
motion.purpose: Ceiling. Nothing in this world runs longer.

motion.name: reduced-motion-clamp
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion clamps every duration here and removes travel — never zero.

narrative.overview:
One warm room, lit two ways. In the day the canvas is warm white and white surfaces float on soft warm-inked shadows; at night it is the same room in warm charcoal, surfaces stepping lighter rather than the palette inverting. Nothing about the geometry, density, or hierarchy changes between them — light and dark are equal citizens, not a theme and its afterthought.

The direction is pinned (user, 2026-08-07): Apple × Airbnb. From Apple come translucent chrome materials, size-specific typography, interruptible motion, and pro-app density — the reference bar is Instruments and Console.app, not a marketing page. From Airbnb come the warmth: warm neutrals rather than blue-grey, generous soft radii, real soft depth, humane row grammar. Explicit anti-references: TUI/terminal aesthetics, themed metaphors, and the discarded Flexoki-plus-shadcn-defaults world that preceded this one.

Motion is part of the world, not decoration. Entrances and state changes ride --ease-out-expo cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (an approximated critically damped spring) or Svelte's quintOut; exits are shorter than entrances (140–160ms out, 180–240ms in); nothing exceeds ~320ms; pointer-down gets feedback before release. prefers-reduced-motion clamps every duration to one 120ms beat and removes travel — it never zeroes durations, because stillness is what the setting asks for, not instant swaps.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral canvas in both modes; a single olive is the only action colour.
Depth from elevation and surface step; hairlines separate, they never outline.
Three status hues reserved for session state, red only where a human is needed.
15px UI base, 12px floor, tracking laddered per size; TX-02 mono for data only.
Three first-class widths: ultrawide (multi-pane, auto-fit tracks), 16" laptop (reference), iPhone (sheets and a thumb bar, never a shrunken desktop).

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Olive means "this acts", and only that. If a surface uses olive for emphasis, ornament, or a chart series that isn't the primary series, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Reserved Hue Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red belong to session state (idle / working / needs-you) and MCP server status. They are never a palette to pick from for a new surface.

rules.name: The Calm Red Rule
rules.body: Red appears only where a human is actually required: a blocked permission, a failed session, the count of either. The attention queue of six blocked sessions is six calm rows with one dot each — never six red banners. Tinted backgrounds stay at 10–15%.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: TX-02 renders code, paths, commands, IDs, and measurements. Never UI labels, never headings, never a costume.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: text-micro (12px) is the smallest text that ships. Nothing renders below it, at any density, on any target.

rules.name: The Tracking-By-Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking is size-specific: negative at display and title, zero at body, positive at caption and micro. Never set a global letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that sits in a column, updates in place, or is compared gets tabular-nums (table and [data-tabular] get it automatically).

rules.name: The Auto-Fit Rule
rules.body: Multi-card boards use auto-fit with a minmax floor, never auto-fill (which pins cards to the floor width and leaves bare tracks on an ultrawide) and never one stretched column.

rules.name: The 36px Row Rule
rules.body: A list row is min-h-9 and reads left to right: state dot, kind glyph, title, path in mono micro, then state word and time pushed right. The hover band is the full card width; the content stops at max-w-3xl. Under pressure the path yields three times as fast as the title and truncates from the left.

rules.name: The No-Outline Rule
rules.body: A surface with a shadow does not also get a border. Cards are rounded-xl bg-card shadow-md, full stop. Hairlines exist to separate siblings inside a card, not to draw its edge.

rules.name: The Night Seam Rule
rules.body: At night the hairline is 5% white — a seam, not an outline. When a control genuinely needs a visible edge in the dark, it takes --input (13%), not a heavier --border.

rules.name: The Ringed Dot Rule
rules.body: A status dot that lands on unknown colour (a favicon, a photo) gets ring-2 ring-background so it reads on anything.

rules.name: The Pill-Control Rule
rules.body: Interactive controls are pills; containers are soft rectangles. Don't square off a button to make it "fit" a card.

dos: Do reach for text-display/-title/-body/-caption/-micro instead of raw text-xs/text-sm — the tracking and the 12px floor live in the utility.
Do build a new floating surface as rounded-xl bg-card shadow-md with no border, and let hairlines separate only what is inside it.
Do put paths, commands, and IDs in font-mono text-micro, and truncate long paths from the left ([direction:rtl] + <bdi>).
Do use ActivityDot for session state and the three status tokens for server status; a hand-rolled coloured dot will drift.
Do check components/ui/ (the full vendored shadcn-svelte kit) and the nearest existing surface before hand-rolling a control.
Do enter at 180–240ms and exit at 140–160ms on quintOut / --ease-out-expo, and pair every pulse with motion-reduce:animate-none.
Do fold a repeating chip row into one counted chip past three items.
Do keep 44pt targets, env(safe-area-inset-*) padding, and 16px inputs on phone surfaces.
Do mark comparable numbers tabular-nums / data-tabular.
donts: Don't use red for anything that is not waiting on the user; a failure that needs no action is muted, not red.
Don't outline a card that already has a shadow, and don't raise the night hairline above 5% to "make it visible".
Don't use dashed borders, hard offset shadows, or striped/diagonal fills to mark ephemerality — side quests are a duotone sparkle plus a "side quest" badge.
Don't set a global letter-spacing, and don't put UI copy in TX-02.
Don't zero durations under prefers-reduced-motion; clamp to 120ms and remove travel, or the comprehension cross-fades go with it.
Don't stretch one column on an ultrawide, and don't ship a shrunken desktop on the phone — the two layouts are different compositions.
Don't hand-paint colours for rendered markdown; .prose is already bound to the tokens in both modes (prose-invert is intentionally a no-op).
Don't animate a state label on first paint.
